item.title: Latvia Keeps AI on the UN Agenda as Drone Threats Intensify Back Home
item.description: Latvia will carry out Europe’s continuing laser focus on emerging technologies by holding its own signature debate this month in the United Nations Security Council as Russia further integrates artificial intelligence into drone strikes targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure in Ukraine. Just this week, Russia launched a “complex massive attack” that included 289 assault drones ... Read more

item.title: Gender equality pays off for business – so why are companies pulling back?
item.description: Gender equality and diversity are good for business – but while increasing numbers of women are reaching top spots in the corporate world, more initiatives are needed to keep momentum going.

item.title: Air raid alerts and attacks on schools: the devastating face of education in Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine has sustained almost 2,000 attacks on education since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, with some 270 this year alone, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday, a day after a strike at a school being used to distribute aid.

item.title: World News in Brief: Children killed in Myanmar strike, new violence flares in Mozambique, an Internet affordability milestone
item.description: A school in Myanmar has been hit in an airstrike, with three children reported killed and five others injured, according to UN Children’s Fund UNICEF.

item.title: Married off at 14: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
item.description: Safa is 14. Her mother died earlier this year. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.

item.title: Haiti gang leader seeks UN talks as El Salvador sends 2,000 troops to hunt for missing soldiers
item.description: A Haitian gang leader wanted by the United States has asked the UN to mediate, as El Salvador sends more than 2,000 troops into the country to search for four of its soldiers who went missing after a gang ambush.
